artworks.title: Head of a Roebuck
artworks.medium: paint (coating), inorganic material, paper, chalk, watercolor (paint)
artworks.description:
The Haarlem artist Wybrand Hendriks tried to render this roebuck’s coat as realistically as possible with delicate dots and lines of the brush. Its dull grey tinge indicates that it is winter, because in the summer the fur is a light brown. The artist undoubtedly had ample time to study the
animal; it is probably dead, lying flat on the ground with lifeless eyes.

artworks.title: Panorama of Cape Town and Environs, Seen from the Sea
artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, ink, pencil, watercolor (paint)
artworks.description: The Dutch East India Company (VOC) also widely engaged in slavery in the southernmost tip of Africa. Enslaved people were shipped from countries around the Indian Ocean to Cape Town. There they worked as domestics and in agriculture to provision the passing VOC ships. Cape Town was also the last place where the Dutch could sell their enslaved servants before heading home.

artworks.title: Harpy Eagle
artworks.description: Like his teacher August Allebé, Bernard Willem Wierink went to Artis Zoo almost daily to sketch all kinds of animals. According to him, the beauty of nature was not solely to be found in a bird of paradise, but also in less attractive animals, such as this ill-tempered looking harpy eagle. The manner in which he drew the lines – first sketchily, and then with greater control and even stylized – is typical of his book illustrations.

artworks.title: Grazing Cow
artworks.description: Jacob Cats greatly admired 17th-century cattle painters, such as Paulus Potter and Adriaen van de Velde. In this drawing he closely imitated his predecessors in this genre and observed the heavy, fleshy cow from a low vantage point. When making the black chalk study from which this finished watercolour was later derived, the artist probably sat in the grass, with a good view of the animal’s solid belly and udders.

Portrait of Joan Jacob Mauricius, Governor-General of Suriname
artworks.description: In this portrait of his friend Mauricius, Troost under-scored their mutual love of the theatre. Mauricius sits in an imaginary interior, with shelves filled with plays behind him. On the wall is Troost’s painting with a scene from the play Jan Claesz of de gewaande Dienstmaagt (Jan Claesz or the Supposed Servant Girl). A drawn self-portrait of Troost hangs over the edge of the table.

artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, watercolor (paint), deck paint, ink
artworks.description: The artist skilfully used only the point of the brush – not a pen – to make this image. He may have copied the porcupine from a watercolour by Joris Hoefnagel preserved in another set of albums once owned by Rudolph II. There is no doubt, however, that this drawing is by De Boodt. It bears a signature, and he added a list at upper left with the animal’s name in eight languages.

artworks.description: Without the representation of the watermelon’s red flesh, this fruit is difficult to identify. The names in the box also provide little clarification. The term ‘pronk appel’ refers to an elongated or spherical, decorative fruit; a pumpkin or gourd, and not strictly a (water)melon. The three growth stages shown demonstrate that the fruit becomes large and heavy. In the case of watermelons, this can sometimes amount to twelve kilograms.

artworks.title: ‘People Are Here Being Crushed for the Love of Art’
artworks.description: To stimulate Dutch art appreciation, Louis Napoleon (the king of Holland between 1806 and 1810) took the initiative of organizing exhibitions of works by contemporary Dutch artists. The first of them, depicted here, was mounted in the Royal Palace on Dam Square and flooded with visitors. On the day of the opening of this exhibition, the palace also opened the Royal Museum, the predecessor of the Rijksmuseum, which was accommodated there as well.

artworks.description:
Witsen’s collection included this album of portraits of successive rulers of the Mughal dynasty. For Witsen, the portraits were a source of knowledge about India’s history. He even had the Persian inscriptions translated by Hendrick Francken, a Protestant minister who had been
posted in Smyrna (now Izmir) for many years. The little portraits were made in Golconda, where Indian miniaturists worked especially for the Europeans who were stationed there because of the textile trade.

artworks.description: This tableau shows the design stages for the book miffy’s letter, in which Miffy goes camping and writes home about her experiences. These black outlines were then transferred to translucent film and placed over various coloured collages.

artworks.title: The Devil Fills the Human Heart with Lust for Riches, Power and Pleasure
artworks.description:
The winged devil is busy painting a shield with depictions of earthly desires: a sack of money, a nude woman, crowns and sceptres. Meanwhile, the young admirer of the diabolical work of art is being shackled. This is Heemskerk’s design for a print engraved by his friend
the printmaker Dirck Volckertsz Coornhert. The same message would later return in the Strong Men: fight the devil and sin with virtuous conduct.

In this drawing Sinibaldo Scorza depicted a scene from the story of Orpheus described by the ancient Roman poet Ovid. The artist filled the sheet from top to bottom with animals from all corners of the world – dromedary can even be spotted in the distance.

artworks.title: Portret van een liggende edelman in een begroeide hof; Portret van Henry Percy, 9th Earl of Northumberland
artworks.description: 'The Wizard Earl'(1564-1632) is gekleed in zwart, de kleur van de magiërs, en steunt eht hoofd in diepzinnig nadenken. Er zijn twee omheinde tuinen en in de boom hangt een  symbolisch teken. De grote rechthoekige tuin staat voor Wetenschap, de kleine voor Filosofie. Aan de boom hangt een bol in evenwicht met een veertje, op ongelijke afstand van elkaar. Deze vormen een rebus: het woord'sphere'(bol) wordt geassocieerd met 'espoir'(hoop) en 'penne'(veer) met  'peine' (verdriet).

artworks.description: Van der Cooghen behoorde tot een groep Haarlemse kunstenaars, die samen naar het leven tekenden en naast zelfportretten ook portretten van elkaar maakten. Hij was hoofdzakelijk tekenaar van figuren, koppen portretten. Zijn tekenstijl is beinvloed door Vlaamse kunstenaars als Rubens en Jordaens, van welke laatste hij een leerling was.

artworks.title: Study of a shell of a tortoise
artworks.medium: paper, materials by function, cartridge paper, paint (coating), ink
artworks.description: At the close of the 16th century, artists became increasingly interested in nature. Jacob de Gheyn’s circle of friends included several scientists. His expertise and excellent observational skills enabled him to portray plants and animals with meticulous accuracy. De Gheyn drew this picture of a tortoise shell from above and the side as a scientist would, observing his subject from different angles.

artworks.title: The Entombment, over a Sketch of an Executioner
artworks.description: This expressive drawing shows how Rembrandt translated his observations of human suffering into the biblical stories he depicted. Christ is truly dead: his body is stiff, and his hair hangs down. The men who carry the cloth with the corpse display visible exertion. Rembrandt initially used this sheet for a sketch of an executioner whose head and arms can still be discerned at the left of the curtain.

The drawing is squared in black chalk so that it can be transferred to a larger format. Perhaps it was intended as a preliminary study for a drawing or painting of larger dimensions

artworks.title: Two Male Heads, Two Arms with a Recorder, and a Child
artworks.description: At the lower right of this study sheet, Watteau depicted two arms and hands holding a recorder. With red chalk alone, the artist exaggerated the bony fingers just enough to capture the delicate tension necessary for playing the instrument. The arms were likely added afterwards to give context to the hands, which explains the anatomically implausible distance between the shoulders.

artworks.title: Venus Urging Cupid to Shoot his Arrow at Pluto
artworks.description:
Venus, the goddess of love, urges her son Cupid to shoot his arrow at Pluto, ruler of the underworld. Pluto thus becomes inflamed with love for Proserpine, the daughter of a god, whom he carries off to his dark underworld kingdom. The drawing served as a model for an engraving by Crispijn van de Passe the Younger. This engraving was part of a series of illustrations
for Ovid’s Metamorphoses.

artworks.title: Aapje zittend op een paal in een bak
Honesty (Lunaria annua)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), inorganic material, materials by function, paper, watercolor (paint), deck paint, chalk, ink
artworks.description: The honesty plant is immediately recognizable by its distinctive flat, and sometimes translucent, seed pods. In this drawing, the plant also bears flowers, something that never occurs simultaneously in reality. De Boodt wanted to give a generic image of the plant in all of its flowering stages, rather than depict a specific specimen from nature. Thus, the drawing was useful in identifying the species.

artworks.description: Algarotti was the leading European art critic and theorist of the mid-18th century, an international celebrity and literary superstar. This portrait was made in 1745 at Venice, where Liotard had been sent by Maria Theresia of Austria and where Algarotti bought his most famous pastel, the Belle chocolatiere for the Elector of Saxony. It was Algarotti’s championing of that work that cemented Liotard’s growing European reputation.

artworks.title: Landscape in Eext (Drenthe Province)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), inorganic material, paper, chalk, watercolor (paint)
artworks.description: Egbert van Drielst was 22 when he moved from the province of Groningen to Amsterdam. As a landscape painter and draughtsman, he found inspiration in the dunes of Haarlem, the heathland of the Gooi district and above all, the still virtually unspoiled country of Drenthe Province. Van Drielst visited Drenthe almost every summer to sketch landscape studies. During the winter, they provided material for his paintings and detailed drawings.

artworks.title: Interior of a Bookshop
artworks.description: Interieur van een vermoedelijk Haarlemse boek- en kunsthandel. Achter de toonbank links de winkelierster met naast haar een jongen die achter een naairaam een boek aan het naaien is. Achter hen stellingen met op de twee bovenste planken voorraden ongebonden papier. Eronder staan gebonden of gebrocheerde boeken, terwijl op de vierde plank van boven vermoedelijk gebonden boeken zijn geplaatst die met de snede en dus met de sloten naar ons toegekeerd zijn. Vooraan tegen de toonbank staan, van links naar rechts, een boek in een blokpers, een klopsteen met een klophamer erop en een lege blokpers. Achter de toonbank rechts de winkelier met een klant. In de kast tegen de achterwand liggen pakken ongebonden boeken (in vellen) of blanco papier en op de bovenste plank staan onder andere globes. Rechts staan twee klanten met (wind?)honden te kijken naar de kunstwerken aan de wand, vermoedelijk schilderijen, prenten en/of tekeningen.

artworks.title: Italian Landscape with Umbrella Pines
artworks.description: Born in southern France and trained in Italy, Fragonard was sensitive to a southern atmosphere. This is masterfully shown here, the golden light of Italy suggested by areas of untouched cream paper. Fragonard rendered the hazy distance of the background with shades of pale brown wash, while accentuating the foreground with undiluted brown ink.

artworks.title: European Hare (Lepus europaeus)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, watercolor (paint), deck paint, ink
artworks.description: In the early 19th century, the mayor of Bruges, Van Huerne, had the Historia Naturalis rebound. The drawings were pasted onto pages provided with framing lines along with the name of each creature inscribed in the Dutch, Latin and French forms of the time. Additionally, he commissioned artists to enhance the drawings by adding surrounding details and backgrounds. As a result, the portrayal of the hare in mid-jump creates the illusion that it is floating above the grass.

Portrait of Amalia Eliza 
Tilanus-van Leeuwen
artworks.description: Amalia Tilanus-van Leeuwen had herself regally portrayed by the most fashionable artist of the time: Thérèse Schwartze. The colourful and detailed likeness is illustrative of Schwartze’s success. With an amazing mastery of pastel, and a hint of flattery, she deftly captured her patron’s character. Tilanus had to splurge for such a magnificent portrait. In keeping with her status as a celebrated portraitist, Schwartze was pricey to say the least.

artworks.title: Man Helping a Rider to Mount a Horse
artworks.description:
Here, Rembrandt was chiefly interested in the rider’s pose. The horse and the man helping the rider are rendered only fragmentarily. Rembrandt corrected himself time and again, scratching over earlier lines with powerful strokes. This probing way of working suggests that he did not have a preconceived image in mind and was giving free rein to his imagination
while drawing.

artworks.description: Around 1600 Anselmus de Boodt compiles several albums for Emperor Rudolf II in which he depicts animals from the imperial menagerie in Prague. While a rhinoceros is missing from this zoo, it nevertheless belongs in these albums which collectively reflect the animal kingdom as it was known at that time. Naturally, De Boodt relies on the image that Dürer had made almost a century earlier.

artworks.title: After the Party
artworks.description: Fortunately Van Looij wrote the title ‘After the party’ on the drawing. A drunken woman in the gutter, her undergarments visible, was a risqué subject in his time. As an artist and writer, Van Looij was fascinated by street parties: his descriptions elucidate how he felt both an ‘aristocratic’ attraction and condemnation. In the excesses of the pleasures of life, the differences between rich and poor vanish and everyone is equal.

artworks.title: Landscape with steep rock formations along a river
artworks.description: De Gheyn adjusted his drawing technique to the size of the paper. He gave form to this landscape with extremely fine lines. He drew a few boats on the water, a mountain hut hidden in the craggy rocks, and a tower with a smoking chimney atop the cliffs. The two figures crossing the wooden bridge are entirely disproportional to the rest of the composition.

artworks.title: Studies of the Mourning Magdalen and the Virgin
artworks.description: In the 1630s Rembrandt painted a series on the suffering of Christ, the Passion. Commissioned by Prince Frederick Henry, the project was discussed via the Prince’s secretary, Constantijn Huygens. Here Rembrandt tried out various poses for the figures of Mary Magdalene (in pen) and the Virgin (in red chalk) in The Entombment. As he later wrote to Huygens, he was seeking the ‘most natural emotions’ of the figures.

artworks.title: A Woman and a Child (Yashoda and Krishna)
artworks.description: The female figure holds her hands above her head, recalling the pose of longing. The small boy next to her raises his hands in order to be lifted up. This composition occurs frequently in Mewari painting from the 15th century onwards. The boy’s blue-grey skin denotes him as Krishna. This portrayal allows the viewer to perceive the Hindu god as an endearing child deserving of unconditional love.

artworks.title: Reclining Youth
artworks.description: Van den Eeckhout was a pupil of Rembrandt from 1635 to 1641. He continued drawing in his master’s style for a long time. He also made a fascinating group of figure studies in brush and wash, the finest of which is this loosely portrayed youth. Such freely drawn studies were undoubtedly the kind of work he preferred making, for at the time, artists likened working for publishers to slave labour.

artworks.title: Prince Eugene of Savoy Vetting a Line-up of Prostitutes
artworks.description: Prince Eugene of Savoy was an impressive general and art collector. According to an old inscription once attached to this drawing, he is seen here with the Amsterdam bookdealer Louis Renard in the exclusive brothel run by Madame Thérèse on Amsterdam’s Prinsengracht. He had the ‘available’ women parade in review, just as he did his own troops. Troost doubtless based his drawing on an anecdote circulating about this at the time.

artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, deck paint, ink
artworks.description: While Rembrandt seldom made specific preparatory designs for his etchings, he occasionally tried out new motifs in drawings. Here, he explored various poses for the sick woman lying before Jesus in the ‘Hundred Guilder print.’ The seated woman on the left keeps her hands lowered, while the other, semi-reclining woman raises one hand to attract Jesus’ attention. In the print, Rembrandt went for a greater dramatic effect, portraying her with barely enough strength to lift her arm.

The sketch of the horse’s head, on the left, has nothing to do with these figures. Rembrandt may have been drawing a horse when he suddenly witnessed and recorded the scene with the woman and child.

artworks.title: Cape Gooseberry or Goldenberry (Physalis peruviana)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), inorganic material, materials by function, paper, watercolor (paint), deck paint, chalk, ink
artworks.description: The fact that the Historia Naturalis albums were sold only three times in four centuries accounts for the excellent condition of the individual drawings. The colours – like the deep orange in this sheet – are as pristine as the day they were applied. This gooseberry may be one of the many botanical drawings in the albums made by the Delft floral painter Elias Verhulst, from whom De Boodt commissioned around 200 drawings.

artworks.title: Peasant Fair
artworks.description: The merry, dancing crowd fills the village square. Yet amid the revelry, things have gotten a bit out of hand: a couple embrace intimately on the left, a man vomits in the centre, and a scuffle brews in the background. The urban couple in the right foreground represents the viewer’s disdain. In the caption, however, the draughtsman Karel van Mander also questions their perceived loftiness.

The Print Seller
artworks.medium: paint (coating), inorganic material, paper, chalk, watercolor (paint)
artworks.description: Two boys peruse prints, while the seller patiently looks on. Will the young connoisseur buy anything? This genre scene is by Jacobus Perkois, founder of the Middelburg drawing academy. In this work he creates a colourful scene using only black and white chalk, with touches in watercolour. The subtle expression on the print seller’s face, as if he were refraining from making any unnecessary comments, demonstrates Perkois’ eye for detail.

artworks.description: De Boodt probably compiled his ‘three large volumes’ as follows: one for plants, one for animals and one for birds. artworks.title: Straatgezicht met doorkijk op de Grote Kerk te Breda
De Strandstraat in Kaapstad
artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, watercolor (paint), ink, pencil
artworks.description:
Gezicht op de Strandstraat in Kaapstad, gezien vanaf de stoep van de lutherse parochiewoning waar Brandes logeerde tussen 20 april en 20 mei 1786. Links is een deel van de stoep te zien. Daarvoor staat een Zwitserse soldaat het pakhuis van de compagnie te bewaken. Op de achtergrond zijn de muren van het kasteel te zien. Boven de huizen van de straat torent de Devil's Peak en het meest zuidelijke punt van de
Tafelberg. In het midden van de straat staat een aantal ossen. Daarachter zijn twee bedienden, of tot slaaf gemaakte mannen, aan het werk. tegenover de parochiewoning staat een man te roken, kijkend naar twee converserende koetsiers.

artworks.title: Susanna and the Elders
artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, deck paint, ink
artworks.description: While bathing, the beautiful Susanna was accosted by two elders, who threatened to accuse her of adultery if she refused their advances. Rembrandt succeeded masterfully in conveying the unsavoury contrast between the position of power of the treacherous men laying their hands on Susanna and her own vulnerability. The man staring intently at her clothing on the ground emphasizes her nudity.

artworks.title: Study of a shell of a tortoise
artworks.medium: paper, materials by function, cartridge paper, paint (coating), ink
artworks.description: At the close of the 16th century, artists became increasingly interested in nature. Jacques de Gheyn’s circle of friends included several scientists. His expertise and excellent observational skills enabled him to portray plants and animals with meticulous accuracy. De Gheyn drew this picture of a tortoise shell from above and the side as a scientist would, observing his subject from different angles.

artworks.title: Study of Tree Trunks and Roots
artworks.medium: coal, organic material, inorganic material, paper, charcoal stick, chalk
artworks.description: Joachim von Sandrart, Savery’s biographer, writes about large trees that the artist drew mit Kohle – in charcoal – in the Tyrol. This is just such a study of trees, indeed drawn in charcoal, which he first soaked in linseed oil. The linseed oil gives the strokes a more saturated black-brown colour, and the pigment adheres better to the paper.

artworks.title: Barn owl (Tyto alba)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), paper, watercolor (paint), deck paint, pencil
artworks.description: The natural science underwent a profound transformation at the end of the 16th century, with greater emphasis placed on insights derived from personal observations. De Boodt, too, adopted a precise and encyclopaedic approach. The artist likely endeavoured to accurately depict this species – like the other owls in the album – on paper. The heart-shaped facial disk and speckled chest of the bird here identify it as a barn owl.

artworks.title: Young Servant Holding a Dish
artworks.description: The graceful and dynamic pose of this figure derives from the fluid outlines. Even though Boucher left out the lower part of his sitter's body, he managed to capture his essence with the elongated fingers, curved back, and head cocked to the side. In his usual manner, Boucher used a lighter red and white chalk to build up the figure's volume.

artworks.title: Longhouse Farmstead with a Haystack in a Polder Landscape
artworks.medium: paper, inorganic material, materials by function, cartridge paper, ink, chalk
artworks.description: Next to a lopsided haystack Rembrandt sketched a ‘langhuisboerderij’ (‘longhouse-farmstead’). These farms contain a dwelling with a fireplace on one side, and a cow shed on the short side. They were made of wood and had thatched roofs, with a smoke hole in the roof ridge. These farms were typical of the area north of the IJ estuary, such as the Zaan region and the small villages in Holland on the Zuiderzee.

added the suggestion of a setting by adding some small strokes in black chalk on the sheet.

artworks.title: The Temple of Vesta in Rome
artworks.medium: paint (coating), mineral, inorganic material, paper, graphite (mineral), watercolor (paint)
artworks.description: The small, round building is traditionally called the Temple of Vesta, incorrectly, as it turns out, for the god to which the temple was consecrated remains unknown. The fact that every detail is fully worked up suggests that the drawing was meant for sale. Still, it does not seem to be fully finished, for Knip would certainly have introduced some colourful accents in the clothing worn by the local folk loitering about.

artworks.title: Top View of a Child’s Fontanel
artworks.medium: paint (coating), watercolor (paint), biological material, parchment (animal material), gouache (paint)
artworks.description: Commissioned by doctors, Jan l’Admiral made detailed anatomical design drawings, of which he later made prints to illustrate their medical treatises. He probably chose parchment because the ‘living’ character of the material suited the subjects. The skull belonged to an unknown child who died before birth. The skin was that of an Ethiopian woman, which begs the question of how the doctors obtained their study materials.

artworks.description: Shortly after Jesus’s birth, an angel appeared to Joseph in a dream, urging him to flee into Egypt with the Virgin and Child. Joseph, with his parted lips and entirely relaxed pose, is clearly sound asleep.

artworks.title: Portrait of Empress Maria Theresa of Austria
artworks.description: It is unclear whether Empress Maria Theresa (1717-1780) is here looking out over the gardens of the Schönbrunn summer residence, which was built during her reign. She wears mourning clothes for the death of her husband, Francis of Lorraine, in 1765. Ignaz Manzador was a Viennese miniature painter. He emphasized the translucent nature of parchment by choosing a double-sided depiction: we see Maria Theresa portrayed from the front and from the back.

artworks.title: Earless seal (Phocidae)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, watercolor (paint), deck paint, ink, pencil
artworks.description: While in Prague, De Boodt could study living animals from distant lands in Rudolf II’s menagerie (zoo) and had access to preserved specimens in the emperor’s Kunstkammer (Cabinet of Curiosities). He also sketched some animals after existing images, such as prints. The detailed rendering of this seal’s rough skin suggests that De Boodt likely saw a real one, probably a taxidermied specimen, as the sea was too far away

artworks.title: Three Orientals Conversing
artworks.description: In Rembrandt’s time, Amsterdam was an extremely cosmopolitan trade centre. Rembrandt was very interested in foreign types, especially in what have long been termed ‘Orientals’. For him, they probably represented biblical figures. He was especially intrigued by their faces and exotic clothing. He recorded them so that he could make the biblical scenes in his paintings and etchings as authentic as possible.

artworks.title: The Elephant Hunt
artworks.description: In addition to cinnamon, elephants were a crucial export for the Dutch. The VOC required the local population to surrender a portion of the cinnamon harvest and assist in elephant hunting. In 1785, VOC official Cornelis de Cock went to see the inland elephant hunt. The Lutheran minister Jan Brandes documented this visit in great detail.

artworks.title: The Aqua Claudia in Rome
artworks.medium: paint (coating), mineral, inorganic material, paper, graphite (mineral), watercolor (paint)
artworks.description: Scattered throughout the ancient city centre of Rome are the remains of the Aqua Claudia. Constructed in the 1st century AD, this aqueduct provided drinking water to large parts of the city. Knip drew the spot where the aqueduct is built over an old city gate not far from the basilica of Santi Giovanni e Paolo.

artworks.title: Oud paar in een nieuw aangelegd park
Marie Congnard-Bathailhy
artworks.dimensions: weight 8.5 kg x height 71.4 cm x width 60.3 cm x thickness 5.5 cm × height 57.5 cm x width 47 cm
artworks.description: This touching and intimate portrait was made towards the end of Liotard’s first sojourn in the Netherlands. The sitter was the 65-year old grandmother of Liotard’s Dutch bride Marie Fargues, a Huguenot like himself, whom he married in Amsterdam in 1756. The virtuoso rendering of the sitter’s black lace pellerine has earned her the sobriquet ‘la dame aux dentelles’.

artworks.title: The farm
artworks.medium: inorganic material, materials by function, paper, ink, chalk
artworks.description: The cottage’s dilapidated roof, the door that has fallen off its hinges, and the broken cartwheel in the foreground attest to this farmstead’s state of disrepair. And no wonder, for the milkmaid and farmhand are clearly idling away their time. The drawing has a deeper meaning: our time on earth is short, so spend it well.

artworks.title: Joseph in Prison Interpreting the Dreams of the Butler and the Baker
artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, deck paint, ink
artworks.description: Joseph was imprisoned thanks to Potiphar’s wife. There he interpreted the dreams of Pharaoh’s butler and baker, fellow inmates. He tells the butler, who listens in amazement, that within three days he will be returned to his job. With his fingers, Joseph counts the days until his release. The standing baker – whose dream means that he will be hanged within three days – has yet to hear his fate.

artworks.title: Seated Actor in the Role of Capitano
artworks.description: Rembrandt’s interest in the theatre lasted throughout his entire career. The costume worn by this actor closely resembles that of the flamboyant, blusterous Capitano, a character in the Italian commedia dell’arte performances and popular in Dutch farces. The woman at the left, an old procuress, offers him an open bag. The Dutch word for ‘bag’ (‘tas’) at the time also meant ‘prostitute’.

artworks.title: Allegory of the Air
artworks.artist: Anselmus Boëtius de Boodt (mentioned on object)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, watercolor (paint), deck paint, ink
artworks.description: As court physician to Rudolf II, known to his contemporaries as ‘the greatest art patron in the world’, De Boodt had access to one of the most spectacular collections of art and curios in Europe. This drawing is based on a painting by Giuseppe Arcimboldo, who served the Hapsburg family for more than 25 years. Appropriately, this Allegory of the Air was included in the album of bird drawings.

artworks.title: Ocean Sunfish (Mola Mola)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), inorganic material, materials by function, paper, pencil, chalk, watercolor (paint), deck paint, ink
artworks.description: The ocean sunfish owes its Latin name Mola, meaning millstone, to its leathery and rough skin. The Dutch name Maanvis, or moonfish, derives from the resemblance between its shape and the celestial body. De Boodt might have seen a stuffed specimen in Emperor Rudolf II’s cabinet of curiosities. Just how large that moonfish was is not clear in this drawing: they can reach a size of 4 metres.

artworks.medium: paper, pasteboard, inorganic material, chalk, cardboard
artworks.description: Because of its biblical subject matter, this drawing by Frans Stamkart can be characterised as Symbolist art. However, the characterisation applies less to the technique, for which Stamkart developed an unorthodox approach of erasing certain passages in chalk. As a result, a soft light seems to break through behind the figure, giving shimmering edges to the swirling clouds, gown and veils.

artworks.description: De Boodt could study many live animals from far-flung places in Emperor Rudolf II’s menagerie. It is not always easy to tell the difference, but the fact that this llama is wearing a collar suggests it was drawn from a live specimen.

artworks.title: Album met 116 tekeningen, hoofdzakelijk portretten, vervaardigd op Ceylon
artworks.medium: textile materials, mineral, biological material, inorganic material, paper, parchment (animal material), silk, chalk, graphite (mineral)
artworks.dimensions: height 16 cm x width 20.6 cm x thickness 3.5 cm
artworks.description: In het tekenboek van Esaias Boursse is vooraan een bladzij meegebonden met de tekst ‘Ik ondergeschreven hebbe dit tijkenboeck op Silon getijkent en verkocht aen mijn broeder tot mijn contentement, den 1 jannewari 1671’. Onder het begrip ‘tekenboek’ kan ook een losse verzameling tekeningen worden verstaan. De meeste tekeningen zijn gemaakt in Ceylon, zoals Sri Lanka tot 1972 heette, terwijl slechts enkele zijn vervaardigd tijdens zijn korte verblijf aan Kaap de Goede Hoop). Het ingebonden ‘Tijkenboeck’ bestaat uit twintig ongelijke katernen, waarvan een aantal incompleet zijn. Het tekenboek bevat nu 116 bladen, maar op zijn minst 34 bladen zijn eerder uitgesneden. Of deze ook tekeningen hebben bevat en waar deze bladen zijn gebleven, valt niet te zeggen – wellicht duiken ze nog eens op. De twee watermerken van het door Boursse gebruikte papier geven aan dat het materiaal hoogstwaarschijnlijk uit Nederland afkomstig was. Boursse kan de dubbelfolio bladen zelf hebben meegenomen, maar het is ook mogelijk dat hij ze op de heenreis in Batavia of tijdens zijn verblijf in Sri Lanka van een medewerker van de VOC heeft gekregen. Het lijkt in ieder geval duidelijk dat hij de grote vellen van ca. 44 x 34,5 cm in de lengte heeft doorgesneden en de twee bladdelen zo gevouwen dat hij er makkelijk buiten mee aan de slag kon. Bij het inbinden, de datum daarvan is niet bekend, zijn de bladen bijgesneden, waardoor in een aantal gevallen de tekeningen niet meer compleet zijn. Misschien is de bundel in handen geweest van een kind van een latere eigenaar, want we zien in een paar onhandige schetsen en toegevoegde woorden. Het ‘Tijkenboeck’ was na het inbinden niet gepagineerd, de nummering van de bladen is van tamelijk recente datum.

artworks.description: This tableau shows the design stages for the book miffy’s letter, in which Miffy goes camping and writes home about her experiences. Once Bruna was satisfied with a sketch, he scored the lines through onto soft paper. He carefully filled the resulting groove with black poster paint, giving rise to a blurred line. These black outlines were then transferred to translucent film and placed over various coloured collages.

Het uiteinde van de slang heeft de vorm van een hand met een roede. Links een draak bij de gebroken Arminiaanse boom. Rechts de stralende Oranjeboom met de deugden Geloof en Gerechtigheid. artworks.title: Portrait of Empress Maria Theresa of Austria
artworks.medium: paint (coating), parchment (animal material), biological material, vellum (parchment), watercolor (paint), gouache (paint)
artworks.description: It is unclear whether Empress Maria Theresa (1717-1780) is here looking out over the gardens of the Schönbrunn summer residence, which was built during her reign. She wears mourning clothes for the death of her husband, Francis of Lorraine, in 1765. Ignaz Manzador was a Viennese miniature painter. He emphasized the translucent nature of parchment by choosing a double-sided depiction: we see Maria Theresa portrayed  from the front and from the back.

artworks.title: Fighting Orchids
artworks.description: Janus de Winter raised a furore around 1916 with depictions of his own feelings – ‘sensations’ – as abstractions. He transformed moods into visionary images for which recognisable motifs were stylised and adapted. His art impressed Theo van Doesburg (1883-1931), founder of De Stijl, who briefly attempted to make abstract art in the manner of De Winter.

artworks.title: Beagle or Braque du Bourbonnais (Canis lupus familiaris)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), paper, watercolor (paint), deck paint, pencil
artworks.description: Hunting was a favorite pastime at the court of Rudolf II, and hunting dogs were an important part of the emperor’s household. The typical stance for these breeds of gundogs is well-observed and captured. The artist skillfully applied colour nuances in the dog’s fur and used the tip of his brush for some white highlights to emphasize his shiny coat.

artworks.title: Kamp van de Arowakken of Caraïben
artworks.description: Bij dit kamp van de Arowakken of Caraïben zijn de hutten heel eenvoudig en dienen voornamelijk als beschutting tegen zon en regen. Het dak van bladeren reikt tot aan de grond. De vloer is de witte zandgrond van de savanne. In de hutten hangen hangmatten. Er is een kookplek naast een van de hutten. Het is niet duidelijk of Huygens hier leden van de stam van de Arowakken of de Caraïben heeft getekend. Beiden horen tot de bevolkingsgroepen die leven aan de benedenloop van de rivieren, in de kuststreek van Suriname. Omdat deze bevolkingsgroepen van oorsprong nomaden zijn, worden hun dorpen ook wel kamp, of kampement genoemd.

artworks.title: Solomon’s Seal (Polygonatum multiflorum)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), inorganic material, materials by function, paper, watercolor (paint), deck paint, chalk, ink
artworks.description: In addition to capturing the white bell-shaped flowers, the draughtsman has gone a step further by including a depiction of the rhizome, typically hidden beneath the ground, from which a new stem sprouts every year. The rhizome is illustrated at the lower right of the drawing. The scars visible where the old stem withers resemble the imprint of a signet ring: specifically, that of the biblical King Solomon, which explains the plant's name.

artworks.medium: paint (coating), inorganic material, materials by function, paper, deck paint, ink, chalk
artworks.description: This drawing is a copy of a close to two-and-a-half metre-wide painting by Rubens that must have originated around 1615. The drawing probably dates from the years shortly thereafter, when the painting was still in Rubens’ workshop. Over a fairly hesitant sketch in black chalk and grey wash, a much more skilful draughtsman – probably Rubens himself – introduced all manner of additions and corrections.

De tekst bestaat uit twee delen: een geschiedenis van het Mogolrijk en de VOC-vestigingen aan de Coromandelkust; daarna volgt een advies aan de Heren XVII over de economische situatie van de VOC in de Coromandel.

artworks.title: Watermill near a Flowing Brook
artworks.description: With his grand visionary landscapes, William Turner would become one of the most important artists of the 19th century. The seed of this development is already contained in this early watercolour. By eliminating clear contours, Turner created a great sense of unity in the scene. He scraped off areas of pigment in places, as a result of which the water of the brook seems to be in constant motion.

artworks.title: View of Luxemburg House at Maarssen on the Vecht
artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, ink, watercolor (paint), pencil
artworks.description: Many of Amsterdam’s wealthy merchants had country estates along the River Vecht, similar to Luxemburg House. In this drawing, artist Hermanus Petrus Schouten depicted the house more meticulously than he usually did in his topographical views. Behind the dark foreground and a corner of some other, smaller country estate lies Luxemburg, bathed in gentle sunlight, on the opposite bank of the Vecht.

artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, deck paint, ink
artworks.description: Portret van Jacob Cats (1577-1660), zittend aan een tafel, wijzend in een boek dat voor hem ligt. Linksachter, op een vensterbank, een zandloper. Door het raam links is de Munnikenhof bij Grijpskerke te zien, Cats' buitenverblijf in de jaren 1603-1623. Vermoedelijk is dit het vroegst bekende portret van de dichter-staatsman. Dat de tekening zeker is bedoeld om in prent te worden gebracht, laat zich afleiden uit het feit dat Cats' familiewapen, rechts onderaan, spiegelbeeldig is afgebeeld. Ontwerp voor een prent.

artworks.title: Panorama van Hottentots Holland
artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, watercolor (paint), ink, pencil
artworks.description: Brandes vervaardigde dit werk toen hij verbleef op de boerderij Vergenoegd: een deel van de boerderij is te zien, namelijk de stenen omheinding en een zonnewijzer. Op de achtergrond zijn de Kaapse bergen (Hottentots Holland Mountains) weergegeven, in het midden is de kloof te zien en de rode aarde van deze doorgang. Uiterst rechts bevindt zich de Valsbaai, helemaal links het plaatsje Stellenbosch (benamingen zijn door Brandes erboven geschreven). Op de voorgrond staan twee boeren te praten, in gezelschap van een hond. Daarachter zijn twee arbeiders weergegeven en links twee figuren op een paard en wagen. Het uitgestrekte vruchtbare landschap, dat door de boerenkolonisten Hottentots Holland werd genoemd, is opgevuld met grazend vee. Links in het landschap zijn ook nog twee boerderijen weergegeven, waarschijnlijk Meerlust en Gedult.

artworks.description: The message of this print series is that existence unfolds in a fixed order, and when complete the cycle begins anew. artworks.title: Smartelijke prinses
artworks.dimensions: height 150 mm x width 101 mm × height 135 mm x width 82 mm
artworks.description: Op een veranda zit een vrouw wat triest voor zich uit te staren. Haar vriendin, die voor haar zit, probeert haar te troosten. Een vrouw, zoals deze, die door haar minnaar in de steek gelaten is, is een bekend thema uit de nayikabheda-literatuur, waarin mannen en vrouwen beschreven en ingedeeld worden al naar gelang hun gedrag en ervaring in de liefde. De voorstelling is opgeplakt op een blad met een smalle sierrand van goud op vergeeld papier, afgezet met zwarte kaderlijntjes; linksboven een stukje opgeplakt.

artworks.title: Vrouwenvertrek te Batavia
artworks.description: Voyeuristische inkijk in een vrouwenvertrek in een woonhuis te Batavia. De vrouw des huizes in slaaphemd in kleermakerszit op de grond, bij haar twee tot slaaf gemaakte bedienden, waarvan een met een sirihdoos en een met een dienblad. De vrouw steekt net iets in haar mond en kijkt op naar een dame met waaier die binnenkomt gevolgd door een tot slaaf gemaakte bediende. Achter een bed met klamboe, links een tafel met een maquette of poppenhuis. Door een gordijn rechts steekt de voyeur zijn hoofd naar binnen.

artworks.title: The abduction of Rukmini by Krishna
artworks.dimensions: height 180 mm x width 261 mm × height 221 mm x width 304 mm
artworks.description: The abduction and forced ‘marriage’ of women is a wellknown motif in Sanskrit literature. A famous example is the abduction of Rukmini by  the god Krishna. The story reflects a cultural milieu, particularly of the warrior caste, in which ideals of masculinity were inextricably linked to expressions of violence and domination. In the case of Krishna and Rukmini, the violence is tempered by a love story.

artworks.title: View of Three Houses on the Surimombo Plantation
artworks.medium: inorganic material, materials by function, paper, ink, chalk
artworks.description: Drawings of the Palmeneribo, Waterland and Surimombo Plantations. With the viewing instructions that Valken burg noted on his drawings, Witsen was able to take a virtual walk around his plantations. There are hardly any people in the drawings, except possibly Valkenburg himself on the doorstep of the residence on Surimombo. The artist seems to have a particular eye for the buildings and for the sluice, which was important to regulate the water level. The sugar cane fields are also missing. For Witsen, Valkenburg was not only a link between the two worlds, but also a filter.

artworks.title: Frost Fair on a Frozen River with Ships
artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, ink, watercolor (paint), pencil
artworks.description: Draughtsman Hendrik Kobell, who died young, drew mainly marine and coastal views with ships. His hometown of Rotterdam had a large harbour, which traded extensively with England and America. After Hendrick Avercamp and Jan van Goyen, frost fairs – with people skating and walking on the ice and food stalls – had become a traditional genre in Dutch art. Kobell’s icebound ships added a new motif to the theme.

artworks.description: Under pressure from fierce opposition to his rule, Stadtholder William V and his family fled The Hague in 1785. They returned two years later and the stadtholder’s authority was restored. This provided the occasion to commission a series of portraits of the members of his family from the portraitist Tischbein. The artist produced a fashionable group of oval portraits in pastel. The giltwood frames were made by the Hague framemaker Hendrik Ebbens.

artworks.title: View of the Residence on the Palmeneribo Plantation
artworks.medium: inorganic material, materials by function, paper, ink, chalk
artworks.description: Drawings of the Palmeneribo, Waterland and Surimombo Plantations. With the viewing instructions that Valken burg noted on his drawings, Witsen was able to take a virtual walk around his plantations. There are hardly any people in the drawings, except possibly Valkenburg himself on the doorstep of the residence on Surimombo. The artist seems to have a particular eye for the buildings and for the sluice, which was important to regulate the water level. The sugar cane fields are also missing. For Witsen, Valkenburg was not only a link between the two worlds, but also a filter.

artworks.title: A Khoikhoi Woman with an Infant
artworks.description: Andries Beeckman (1628-1664). Andries Beeckman recorded the people he saw on his travels to South Africa and Southeast Asia. As far as we know he drew them from life. Only he probably did not see the Khoikhoi woman with an infant in this way, as he copied her from a drawing in an English travel journal. Beeckman’s drawings found favour with European collectors and he also used them as preliminary studies for his paintings.

artworks.description: In Batavia, a visit to the market was often accompanied by a performance. A wayang show is in progress in a richly decorated theatre. Wayang literally means shadow or phantom. It comprises all kinds of Javanese theatre forms such as puppetry and shadow play, but also dance, drama and elocution. Schouten noted below his drawing that he had seen it during the day, whereas it was usually held in the evening until early morning.

artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, ink, watercolor (paint)
artworks.description: Vrouw, op de rug gezien, lopend naar links, met op het hoofd een beschilderde hoed: 'Chapeau peint en Coquille'. Zij draagt een japon met korte mouwen en sleep. Op de achterzijde van de mouw een zig-zag versiering. Verdere accessoires: om de schouders een sjaal afgezet met franjes, waaier, lage schoenen met puntige neuzen. In de rechterhand een bloem. Links een opspringend hondje met halsband. Voortekening voor prent 215 in Journal des Dames et des Modes, Costume Parisien, 10 mai 1800, An 8, uitgegeven door Pierre de la Mésangère, Parijs, 1797-1839.

Closely watched by the bust of her stepfather, Napoleon, Queen Hortense is reading Thérèse philosophe, a pornographic novel, with her hand wandering under her dress and her bottom exposed to the fire. This obscene political caricature mocks the sexual appetite of Louis Bonaparte’s
wife, briefly Queen of Holland (1806–1810), who was known for her numerous extramarital affairs.

artworks.title: In the Environs of Genzano
artworks.medium: paint (coating), mineral, inorganic material, paper, graphite (mineral), watercolor (paint)
artworks.description: Just like many other artists, Knip fled from the oppressive heat in the Eternal City in the summer months and sought relief in the cooler hills east of Rome. Here he portrayed the surroundings of Genzano, a little town near Lake Nemi. Knip’s inscription on the drawing does not tell us precisely what he drew, possibly a monastery with buildings around a courtyard, and a church at the left.

artworks.title: Gallerie des Modes
artworks.description: In 1778 two young publishers tapped a previously undiscovered market with the launch of a series entitled Gallerie des Modes, which responded to the growing demand among Parisians for fashion news. Initially featuring only hairstyles, the series’ illustrations were later extended to include complete outfits to cater to its audience. These showed figures from head to toe. All ranks of French society were represented in a wide variety of fashionable clothes, from the simple negligée 1 to the robe à la polonaise 2 3, the robe à l’anglaise 4 and the occasional smart gentleman’s suit.

artworks.title: Black Crowned Crane (Balearica pavonina)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), inorganic material, materials by function, paper, watercolor (paint), deck paint, pencil, chalk, ink
artworks.description: De Boodt probably assembled his ‘three large books’ as follows: one for plants, one for animals and one for birds. The latter was apparently damaged (many of the bird studies have a loss at one corner), which may have prompted the 19th-century remounting campaign. Here the lower right corner is missing, but this pavo sine cauda chinensis (literally: ‘peacock without Chinese tail’) – with its gold, feathered ‘crown’ – remained unaffected.

artworks.title: Plundering Soldiers near a Cottage
artworks.description: The world we enter here is quite different from Adriaen van de Velde’s sunny, carefree Dutch Arcadia. This is the world of military mayhem, death, and plundering. In Van de Velde’s time this world was always close by: throughout most of the 17th century parts of Europe were stricken by seemingly neverending acts of war.

artworks.title: Town Square with Fair
artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, ink, watercolor (paint), pencil
artworks.description: Johannes Huibert Prins compiled this majestic imaginary town square by combining various actual and fictitious buildings. He drew the figures with meticulous precision, as well as the façades, the cobblestones and even the grouting of the brickwork. Some contemporaries thought the detail a little overdone. For example, one critic wrote in 1817 that Prins had rendered the masonry too elaborately and that it never really looked like that when reduced in size.

artworks.title: Voorde aan de rand van een bos
Snow Bunting (Plectrophenax nivalis)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), paper, watercolor (paint), deck paint, pencil
artworks.description: While in Prague, De Boodt could study living animals from distant lands in Rudolf II’s menagerie (zoo). He also had access to preserved specimens in the emperor’s Kunstkammer (Cabinet of Curiosities). Additionally, he relied on existing images to depict certain creatures. In the case of this snow bunting, De Boodt could simply observe it in the wild. Although the songbird breeds in the far northern regions of the world, it migrates south during the winter, including areas near Prague.

artworks.title: Study of Apple Blossom, Dead Nettle, Mayflower, and Ground Ivy
artworks.description: Nieuwenhuis’ drawn studies of flowers and plants formed the basis of the lithographs used to illustrate articles about Dutch flora. The contours are even more distinctive because the artist set the plants against a black background.

artworks.title: Sluice on the Palmeneribo Plantation
artworks.medium: inorganic material, materials by function, paper, ink, chalk
artworks.description: Drawings of the Palmeneribo, Waterland and Surimombo Plantations. With the viewing instructions that Valken burg noted on his drawings, Witsen was able to take a virtual walk around his plantations. There are hardly any people in the drawings, except possibly Valkenburg himself on the doorstep of the residence on Surimombo. The artist seems to have a particular eye for the buildings and for the sluice, which was important to regulate the water level. The sugar cane fields are also missing. For Witsen, Valkenburg was not only a link between the two worlds, but also a filter.

artworks.description: In a succinct biography of 1819 Knip wrote: ‘I set out for Naples on 6 September 1811, and having seen the most beautiful sights I returned to winter in Rome with a good portfolio (of drawings) from that beautiful region.’ He more than likely made his drawings of Mount Vesuvius on this trip. artworks.description: This quick scribble almost certainly shows Rembrandt’s wife, Saskia, whom he often drew during her confinements and illnesses. A very similar drawing, now in London, depicts the same woman holding a baby. Because Rembrandt favoured red chalk in the mid-1630s, that baby is most likely Rembrandt and Saskia’s firstborn son, Rumbartus, who was baptized on 15 December 1635 and died two months later.

artworks.medium: paint (coating), inorganic material, materials by function, paper, deck paint, watercolor (paint), chalk, ink
artworks.description:
A largely youthful crowd has gathered to watch two men scrape a pig’s carcass before butchering it. After 1672, Adriaen van Ostade focused increasingly on drawings rather than his more labour-intensive and expensive paintings. Presumably he was responding to the rising demand for cheaper products among the more careful collectors following the disastrous year 1672, when war had tipped the Dutch Republic into
an economic crisis.

The subject of this watercolour is derived from the poem The Curfew. In the poem, a lonely man hears the curfew ringing across the water. Varley worked primarily in watercolour. He strove to make his watercolours as large, and as aspiring in
content, as paintings in oil. The particular beauty of watercolours, according to him, lay in the panoramic rendering of the ‘clear skies, distances and water’.

artworks.title: De Slag bij Solebay, 7 juni 1672, even na twee uur in de middag, gezien vanuit het noordwesten: rechterdeel
artworks.medium: materials by function, paper, ink, pencil
artworks.description: De Slag bij Solebay, 7 juni 1672, even na twee uur in de middag, gezien vanuit het noordwesten: rechterdeel. Deze uit twee delen bestaande tekening geeft een moment uit de Slag van Solebay in 1672 weer. In dit openingsgevecht van de derde Engelse Zeeoorlog vocht de Staatse vloot onder leiding van admiraal De Ruyter tegen de gecombineerde Engels-Franse vloot voor de kust van Suffolk, ter hoogte van Solebay. Net als bij eerdere zeeslagen voer Willem van de Velde aan boord van zijn galjoot aan Nederlandse zijde mee. De zeeslag is in volle gang. Het linkerblad toont onder meer de Dolfijn, het schip van luitenant-admiraal Willem Joseph, baron Van Ghent die bij deze slag om het leven zou komen. Het brandende schip Royal James staat deels op het linker- en deels op het rechterdeel. Dit fregat van admiraal Edward Mountagu, Earl of Sandwich, werd omstreeks twee uur in de middag door een Hollandse brander geraakt. De Royal Prince, het vlaggeschip van de hertog van York dat al voor de middag zo beschadigd werd dat de hertog zijn vlag moest overbrengen naar de St. Michael, was oorspronkelijk door Van de Velde rechtsboven de zuidas van de windroos geplaatst, maar werd door hem met een stukje papier weer afgedekt.

artworks.title: Kneeling Man in a Turban and Heavy Robes
Warmond Castle
artworks.description: In this drawing Roghman presents Warmond Castle as a mighty fortress. Two imposing towers flank the castle, which is built in various styles. By portraying the structure so expansively, Roghman left little room for its surroundings. He depicted only the dog slumbering in the foreground, a stray or perhaps the pet of Jacob van Wassenaer Warmond and his wife.

artworks.artist: Anselmus Boëtius de Boodt (signed by artist)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, watercolor (paint), deck paint, pencil, ink
artworks.description: De Boodt could study many living animals from distant places in Rudolf II’s menagerie (zoo). He could have seen mounted specimens in Rudolf’s Kunstkammer. Yet some animals were ‘borrowed’ from illustrations by other artists. Could De Boodt have been looking at a live or stuffed specimen? Or did he copy it? In any case, the dark brown plumage and the beautiful ‘white drops’ are convincingly rendered.

artworks.title: De Slag bij Solebay, 7 juni 1672, even na twee uur in de middag, gezien vanuit het noordwesten: linker deel
artworks.medium: materials by function, paper, ink, pencil
artworks.description: De Slag bij Solebay, 7 juni 1672, even na twee uur in de middag, gezien vanuit het noordwesten: linkerdeel. Deze uit twee delen bestaande tekening geeft een moment uit de Slag van Solebay in 1672 weer. In dit openingsgevecht van de derde Engelse Zeeoorlog vocht de Staatse vloot onder leiding van admiraal De Ruyter tegen de gecombineerde Engels-Franse vloot voor de kust van Suffolk, ter hoogte van Solebay. Net als bij eerdere zeeslagen voer Willem van de Velde aan boord van zijn galjoot aan Nederlandse zijde mee. De Slag bij Solebay is in volle gang. Het linkerblad toont onder meer de Dolfijn, het schip van luitenant-admiraal Willem Joseph Baron Van Ghent die bij deze slag om het leven zou komen. Het brandende schip Royal James staat deels op het linker- en deels op het rechterdeel. Dit fregat van admiraal Edward Mountagu, Earl of Sandwich, werd omstreeks twee uur in de middag door een Hollandse brander geraakt. De Royal Prince, het vlaggeschip van de hertog van York dat al voor de middag zo beschadigd werd dat de hertog zijn vlag moest overbrengen naar de St. Michael, was oorspronkelijk door Van de Velde rechtsboven de zuidas van de windroos geplaatst, maar werd door hem met een stukje papier weer afgedekt.

artworks.title: An Ambonese Dancing Warrior in a Blue Robe

In zijn linkerhand houdt hij een 'salawaku', een ceremonieel Moluks schild uit één stuk hout, en in zijn linkerhand een 'parang'een gekromd zwaard. Hij voert een 'cakalele', een Molukse krijgsdans, uit.

artworks.title: View of Moel Siabod from Beddgelert, North Wales
artworks.description:
Cornelius Varley was a scientist by profession. He painted watercolours above all for his own pleasure. Between 1800 and 1805 he produced a series of sensitive studies of nature, which he often deliberately left unfinished and devoid of detail.
Already in Varley’s own time other artists greatly admired these unconventional works, which were thus of seminal importance for English landscape art.

artworks.description: Natural science changed dramatically towards the end of the 16th century, with greater emphasis placed on insights derived from personal observations. However, the draughtsman seems to have made a mistake: this squid has one tentacle too many.

artworks.title: A Sculpture Group in the Garden of Honselaarsdijk Castle
artworks.description: A large number of landscape drawings by De Bisschop have been preserved, almost all of which are in a small format. Many of these drawings were made during excursions in the surroundings of The Hague. Honselaarsdijk Castle was located near Naaldwijk, southwest of The Hague. Using powerful contrasts of light and shade, the draughtsman effectively conveyed the play of sunlight on the trees and the sculpture group.

artworks.title: Colombo
artworks.description: Colombo, Gallen, and Jaffna were the most important towns for the VOC on Sri Lanka. The first sight to greet those approaching Colombo from the sea was the governor’s residence, with a church and the VOC’s adjacent wharf. Behind the palace sprawled a large garden where vegetables were grown.

artworks.title: The Drummer

Perhaps the drawings were intended for a series of prints, however the plan was never realized. These sets were known as ‘street cries’, after the way the hawkers shouted out their wares and services.

The smoking volcano and the cool stones still seem tangible more than three centuries later. The artist worked from dark to light in order to capture the evening atmosphere. The colour white is reserved for the sparsely shining moonlight and the rippling water.

artworks.title: Napoleons verbanning naar Elba, 1814
artworks.description: Spotprent op de verbanning van Napoleon naar het eiland Elba, mei 1814. Napoleon wordt zittend in een kooi door twee Engelse matrozen naar een wachtende sloep gebracht, daarachter wachten twee Britse transportschepen. Op het land blijven achter: een Oosterse man, de keizerin gekleed in lompen, vier Franse oorlogsinvaliden die nu op straat hun kost verdienen met straatorgel, triangel en marmotten. Op een heuvel zweren in een tent de maagden van de vijf bondgenoten boven een brandend altaar elkaar trouw. In de lucht een ruiter op het gevleugelde paard Pegasus.

artworks.description: The halo pattern that was the starting point for the adjacent necklace also features in other of Lauweriks’ jewellery designs. artworks.title: De eerste koninginne van den Mogol Auxeng Zeeb
artworks.description: Tekening uit het manuscript van de VOC dienaar Adrianus Canter Visscher met achterin achtentwintig Indiase miniaturen en twee kaarten van plaatsen aan de Coromandelkust. Spotprent op Napoleons verbanning naar Elba, 1814
artworks.description: Spotprent op Napoleons verbanning naar Elba, mei 1814. Geboeid wordt Napoleon op kar gemend door de duivel afgevoerd. De duivel zit op een stapel dooshoofden. Een vrouw houdt Napoleon een fles onder de neus terwijl zij hem met een roede afranselt, zij draagt bij zich een doosje met een marmot. De wagen wordt getrokken door de vier broers van Napoleon en voorafgegaan door generaal Ney, gekleed in lompen. Vooraan loopt een zwijn met keizerskroon en scepter. Achter de wagen vier geboeide Franse generaals. Op de voorgrond lopen met de wagen mee: ratten, een slang, pad, draakje en hagedis. Staande op een heuvel op de achtergrond vier vaandrigs van Rusland, Pruisen, Nederland en Groot-Brittannië, boven hen blaast de Faam op haar bazuin.

artworks.title: Portrait of a Young Woman
artworks.description: Ottavio Leoni was a popular portraitist among Rome’s most prominent families. However, he also drew ordinary people, such as this likeness of an unknown young woman. He depicted her face and loosely bound up hair with great precision, while sketching her body with just a few strokes. He had learnt this accuracy from his father, a medallist by profession.

artworks.medium: paper, materials by function, prepared paper, paint (coating), ink
artworks.description: Why this boy is holding a stick is unclear. Rembrandt may have portrayed a victim of leprosy, who was required to carry a stick to warn his healthy fellow citizens. Rembrandt deliberately did not draw the stick entirely straight, giving it a more natural appearance. He used iron gall ink, notorious for eating holes through paper, so-called ink corrosion.

artworks.title: Sultan Conrom
artworks.description: Tekening uit het manuscript van de VOC dienaar Adrianus Canter Visscher met achterin achtentwintig Indiase miniaturen en twee kaarten van plaatsen aan de Coromandelkust. De tekst bestaat uit twee delen: een geschiedenis van het Mogolrijk en de VOC-vestigingen aan de Coromandelkust; daarna volgt een advies aan de Heren XVII over de economische situatie van de VOC in de Coromandel.

artworks.title: De doktersvisite aan de keizer
artworks.date: in or after 1734 - in or before 1736
artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, watercolor (paint), ink
artworks.description: Ontwerp voor een kop en schotel met Chinees motief in opdracht van de Verenigde Oost-Indische Compagnie. Binnen een cirkel waarin een zesarmige waaiervorm is opgenomen, zitten drie mannen op een bank rond een tafel. Eén van hen houdt een vis vast. Op de tafel staat een grote schaal en links kijkt een pauw op naar een vogel op de overhangende tak van een boom. De ruimten tussen de zes armen zijn opgevuld met een geometrisch motief. Boven het ontwerp is het zijaanzicht van zowel de kop als de schotel afgebeeld. Behalve een rand met een geometrisch motief is de schotel voor het overige blanco. Op het kopje is opnieuw de voorstelling met de drie mannen afgebeeld.

artworks.description: Chand Bibi of Ahmadnagar (16th century) is one of the few queens who successfully wielded power. She protected her kingdom from the Mughal imperial armies. There are no surviving pictures of her made during her lifetime, but the valiant warrior queen became a favourite subject in the 18th century. She is almost always depicted hawking and never while defending the city of Ahmadnagar, her main feat of arms.

artworks.title: View of Ariccia from Genzano
artworks.medium: paint (coating), mineral, inorganic material, paper, graphite (mineral), watercolor (paint)
artworks.description:
Knip drew the town of Ariccia and environs as seen from Genzano on two sheets of paper. Ariccia is dominated by the dome of the church of Santa Maria dell’Annunziata, designed by Bernini. At the right is the Santuario di Santa Maria di Galloro, where a miraculous image of the Virgin Mary, painted on a piece of rock, has been venerated since 1623. In the foreground Knip twice drew a detail of an old paved road,
probably the Appian Way.

artworks.medium: paint (coating), mineral, inorganic material, paper, graphite (mineral), watercolor (paint)

excavated from 1824, a process that continued long into the 20th century.

artworks.title: Nude Young Man, Half Length
artworks.medium: paper, inorganic material, prepared paper, chalk
artworks.description: Rembrandt trained with Lastman around 1624. In that period, as preparation for his history pieces, Lastman drew figure studies in red chalk on paper that he had coloured yellow. This technique appealed to Rembrandt. During and shortly after his apprenticeship, Rembrandt made multiple drawings in red chalk on prepared paper. Years later he even owned a ‘boeckie vol schetsen […] met rood krijt’ (little book full of sketches […] in red chalk) by Lastman.

artworks.title: The Breach in the Saint Anthony’s Dike near Amsterdam
artworks.description: Jan van Goyen must have visited the site of the disaster shortly after it occurred. He recorded the breach in the dike and the flooded countryside in a sketchbook that was disassembled centuries later. This detailed drawing is based on one of those small sketches. For unknown reasons, he added leaves to the trees here, even though at the beginning of March they would still have been bare.

artworks.title: Een man doet hurkend zijn behoefte
Piazza San Marco, Venice, Seen from the South-west
artworks.medium: mineral, inorganic material, materials by function, paper, graphite (mineral), chalk, ink
artworks.description: In the 18th century, Rome and Venice were flooded with tourists, mainly from England. Canaletto took full advantage of this with his charming drawn or painted cityscapes depicting the famous Venetian monuments. He probably sold his drawings as souvenirs while working on the streets. ‘By chance’ he would have with him a portfolio with all sorts of cityscapes he had previously drawn in his studio.

artworks.description: John Law gezeten in een rinkelstoel voor het Lazarushuis krijgt van gebochelde Bombario eten en drinken aangereikt. Op de voorgrond deelt een aap aandelen uit, rechts kinderen met een molentje, links een wanhopige windhandelaar. Op de achtergrond wordt een gek geworden actionist naar het gekkenhuis gebracht. Ontwerptekening voor een niet uitgevoerde prent in een serie over de opkomst en ondergang van Quincampoix (John Law). Bij de tekening behoort een uitleg. Behoort tot de groep van tekeningen toegevoegd aan de serie Tafereel der Dwaasheid met spotprenten op de Windhandel of Actiehandel van 1720.

artworks.title: Reclining Female Nude
artworks.medium: coal, organic material, paper, charcoal stick
artworks.description: This drawing looks like it was executed in mere minutes. Indeed, Israëls was more interested in capturing the essence of the pose than in producing a detailed depiction. For these kinds of drawings Israëls almost always used charcoal or chalk, which allowed him to work swiftly. Moreover, the charcoal did not adhere everywhere on the grainy surface of the paper, whereby the drawing seems to capture the light.

artworks.title: Standing Female Nude with Raised Arm
artworks.description: Aert de Gelder drew the contour of the posing model with swift, angular pen lines. He had learned to draw this way in Rembrandt’s workshop, where he apprenticed at the beginning of the 1660s. Typical for De Gelder, however, are the passages of shade on the woman’s legs, stomach and breasts. They lend the figure a certain plasticity against the virtually undefined background.

artworks.title: Festive Peasants, Soldiers, and Harlots
artworks.description:
While a soldier is amorously engaged, a peasant pinches his jug of beer. Meanwhile a harlot robs the peasant of his money, unaware that a soldier is cheating by looking at her hand of cards. Vinckboons made the drawing on the eve of the Twelve Year Truce (1609-1621) marking the cease-fire between Spain and the Northern Netherlands. In the seeming reconciliation, he perceives the seeds of new conflicts in
the future.

artworks.title: Farmhouse with a Well
artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, watercolor (paint), ink
artworks.description: When Adriaen van Ostade died, Cornelis Dusart inherited the studio’s contents from his master. This included drawings by Adriaen’s brother, Isaac. Dusart made this landscape after one of Isaac’s drawings. Dusart’s copy is less detailed and a little dull compared to the original. Whether Dusart drew these copies purely to practise or perhaps to pass them off as genuine Van Ostades is no longer known.

He also commissioned artists to add surrounding details and a background to the drawings. As a result, this donkey ended up standing on a grassy patch.

Bird of paradise (Paradisaea apoda)
artworks.artist: Anselmus Boëtius de Boodt (signed by artist)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, watercolor (paint), deck paint, ink
artworks.description: The myth that birds of paradise never had any feet and thus spent their life in perpetual flight goes back to ancient times. This draughtsman seems to have believed that as well. Even the 18th-century French inscription, sans pattes (without feet), emphasizes this apparent feature. In reality, the feet were removed by the local traders who sent the stuffed birds from Asia to Europe.

artworks.description: Even though this is one of his earliest drawings, the teenage Paulus Potter nevertheless portrayed the anatomy of the cow’s body with consummate skill. In this drawing the same standing cow is seen from the back, the side, and the front.

artworks.description: Fat buttocks and fleshy folds may well be typical features of Rubens’ beauty queens, but most women today by far favour the ideal of thinness. Despite the counter-movement introduced by Kim Kardashian, having a ‘fat ass’ is still not considered a compliment. Kooi sees this differently. She presents the female derrière together with a plump, stuffed sausage surrounded by rotund curves like jewels in satin-lined boxes.

artworks.description: Unlike most Italian artists, Castiglione was strongly influenced by foreign art. In his hometown of Genoa he came into contact with the work of Peter Paul Rubens. He also spent some time there in the studio of Anthony van Dyck. That Flemish influence is clearly reflected in this drawing: the striking use of colour and the animated composition recall oil sketches by Rubens and Van Dyck.

artworks.title: Vamana (Trivikrama) avatar
artworks.description: Vamana (de kleine mens) is de vijfde incarnatie (avatara, letterlijk: 'nederdaling') van Vishnu. In een gevecht tussen de goden en de demonen hebben de goden het onderspit gedolven. Vishnu verschijnt dan in de gedaante van een kleine mens en vraagt de koning van de demonen, Bali, om een klein stukje grond die hij in drie stappen kan betreden. Bali stemt in. Vishnu verandert in een reuzenfiguur en stapt over de aarde, de onderwereld en over de hemelen. Volgens een andere overlevering met een stap verovert hij de hemel en de aarde, met de tweede stap het universum. Omdat er geen plaats is voor de derde stap, biedt Bali zijn eigen hoofd aan. Deze vorm van Vishnu wordt ook Trivikrama (Sanskrit: drie stappen) genoemd.

artworks.title: Aristolochiaceae?

artworks.description: The natural sciences underwent a profound transformation at the end of the 16th century, with greater emphasis placed on insights derived from personal observations. De Boodt, too, adopted a precise and encyclopaedic approach. In this case, the artist may have studied a species from the Birthwort family, recognizable by its tubular flower – a notorious trap for insects – and its spherical fruit. The drawing does not appear entirely lifelike, making the genus of the plant unclear.

artworks.description: The natural sciences underwent profound change at the end of the 16th century. From then on, personal observation and experimentation were certainly just as important as ancient writings. Illustrated albums and books to convey this new visual information had to be compiled and written. De Boodt set about this encyclopaedically. He recorded rare specimens as well as more commonplace species, like these weasels, with astonishing accuracy.

artworks.title: Mountain Landscape with Ruins
artworks.description: This is clearly an imaginary scene: the artist has situated the Temple of Minerva Medica in a ghostly and misty mountain landscape, while in reality it is located in Rome. Paulus van Vianen based the rendering of the ancient temple on a print, for he did not know the building first-hand. He never went to Rome.

artworks.title: Visit to the Zoo
artworks.medium: inorganic material, materials by function, paper, ink, chalk
artworks.description: In the 19th century, zoos and menageries were often accessible only to artists and the well-to-do. Elegantly dressed ladies and gentlemen with top hats went there to parade; the animals were simply part of the background scenery. However, in this drawing the roles are reversed. One of the monkeys has gotten hold of a hat, startling a group of distinguished visitors.

artworks.title: An African Woman with a Hand Drum
artworks.description: Andries Beeckman (1628-1664). Andries Beeckman recorded the people he saw on his travels to South Africa and Southeast Asia. As far as we know he drew them from life. Only he probably did not see the Khoikhoi woman with an infant in this way, as he copied her from a drawing in an English travel journal. Beeckman’s drawings found favour with European collectors and he also used them as preliminary studies for his paintings.

artworks.description: Bruna’s artistic ambitions encountered resistance at home. As a compromise, he began designing book covers for the family publishing company. Looking back, he was grateful for this development; he realized that the restrictions such designs placed on him had been crucial to his creative development. Between 1951 and 1969 he designed over 2000 book covers. He cut, tore, drew, glued, photographed and painted, inspired by modern French artists.

artworks.title: Jack by the Hedge (Alliaria)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), inorganic material, materials by function, paper, watercolor (paint), deck paint, chalk, ink
artworks.description: It is unclear where the name ‘Jack by the hedge’ came from. It is thought that it may stem from the slang ‘jacks’ for toilet due to its smell; when rubbing the leaves the plant releases a garlicky smell. Despite its other nickname, hedge garlic, it is botanically unrelated to garlic species. However, it was and still is often used in cooking.

artworks.title: Seated Man Smoking a Pipe by Candlelight while Houses Outside Are Ablaze
artworks.description: This man smokes his a pipe contentedly at home while a fire rages outside. What Troost was trying to convey with this depiction is not entirely clear. A man warming himself by the heat of another man’s blazing house was considered a symbol of Selfishness in the 16th century. In the 18th century, Troost was known for his satirical approach, ridiculing life in and outside the sitting room.

artworks.medium: biological material, inorganic material, parchment (animal material), chalk
artworks.description: Cornelis Visscher drew this young woman with coarse as well as very fine hatching in black chalk. Its message, in combination with the skull, the statuette of Time, and the broken glass, could not be clearer: life is finite.

artworks.title: ‘Eruditio Musica, Solo Sung by Madame Colin’
artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, deck paint, watercolor (paint), ink
artworks.description: Andriessen and his family regularly attended concerts by the Eruditio Musica Orchestra in the High German Theatre in Amsterdam. On this evening, Joseph Haydn’s The Seasons was performed, a musical composition that at that time was not even eight years old. A certain ‘Madame Colin’ sang a solo. The audience’s casual mood is striking. Two gentlemen converse in the left foreground, while another one steps unabashedly over a bench at the right.

artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, watercolor (paint), deck paint, pencil, ink
artworks.description: De Boodt probably compiled his ‘three large albums’ as follows: one for plants, one for animals, and one for birds. The bird album was damaged, which may explain why all the drawings were rebound in the early 19th century. Only the branch, on which this great spotted woodpecker perches, was affected. The bird itself – identified by the red spot on its head as a male – was left unscathed.

artworks.title: Residence and a Barn on the Surimombo Plantation
artworks.medium: inorganic material, materials by function, paper, ink, chalk
artworks.description: Drawings of the Palmeneribo, Waterland and Surimombo Plantations. With the viewing instructions that Valken burg noted on his drawings, Witsen was able to take a virtual walk around his plantations. There are hardly any people in the drawings, except possibly Valkenburg himself on the doorstep of the residence on Surimombo. The artist seems to have a particular eye for the buildings and for the sluice, which was important to regulate the water level. The sugar cane fields are also missing. For Witsen, Valkenburg was not only a link between the two worlds, but also a filter.

artworks.title: Kneeling Female Nude with Outstretched Arms
artworks.description: Aert de Gelder made this nude study during his pupillage with Rembrandt. Like his master, his rendering of the posing woman with drooping breasts and a sagging stomach is unvarnished. It was only in Rembrandt’s workshop that drawing after a nude female model became more prevalent among Dutch artists. Not only was it an excellent exercise, but studies of nudes also often served as models for figures in a painting.

artworks.title: A Father Should Surround His Child with Love and to Protect and Eclipse Him with His Devotion and Righteousness
artworks.description: Elisabeth Stoffers is one of the few women who turned to abstraction early on. Her work expresses sympathy for the astral world that exists alongside of, and after, physical life. This astral world can be experienced during dreams, and out of the body and near-death experiences. Her pastel drawings also evince a relationship with the abstractions and the colours of energy fields around human beings, as illustrated in the plates of theosophical books of the time.

artworks.description: Geschilderd en geplakt beeldverhaal met autobiografische overpeinzingen van de kunstenaar over de zin van kunst en kunstenaarschap. De tekst begint met: “…Ik zat strontziek thuis … als een dodelijk verveelde Baselitz hing ik mezelf vleermuisgelijk aan het plafond op om te ontkomen besloot ik in gedachten te verdwijnen“.
