In the 18th century a visit to a flower nursery was a popular spring outing. Fashionably attired ladies and gentlemen here stroll past seed boxes and racks with potted plants. People from Amsterdam, Leiden, and The Hague all came for this purpose to Haarlem, the centre of floristry.
This drawing is an illustration of the month of April from a series of the Twelve Months.

artworks.title: Woman with Two Baskets of Fruit and a Cherry Branch
artworks.medium: paint (coating), keratinous material, feather (material), biological material, materials by function, paper, pen (veer), ink, watercolor (paint)
artworks.description: The motto at the bottom of the sheet explains the connection between the drawing of a woman carrying fruit and Jacob Cats’ poem about chastity. After all, it is better to pick fruit yourself than to accept ‘pearsthat have already been plucked,’ alluding to promiscuity.  In this early drawing, Gesina ter Borch opted for a simple illustration to accompany the text. Years later, in her Poëzie-album (Poetry Album), she would  provide the same poem with a more complex composition.

Mole (Talpaeuropaea) and Shrew-mouse 
(Soricidae)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, watercolor (paint), deck paint, pencil, ink
artworks.description: Contrary to what its name suggests, the shrew-mouse does not belong to the rodent family, like mice, but to the mole family. Like moles, shrews eat insects: larvae, worms, snails and sometimes spiders. Both animals are mainly active at night. During these nocturnal hours the mole in particular digs underground tunnels, which the shrew with its shorter legs makes good use of.

artworks.artist: Johan Daniël de Gijselaar (signed by artist)
artworks.description: In een burgerlijke woning zitten drie Franse soldaten aan een tafel te roken en te drinken. Een vierde staat bij de schouw met open haardvuur. De dienstmeid staat voor de tafel en maakt het gebaar 'betalen'. De soldaten lachen haar uit. Aan de muur van het vertrek een tekening met dezelfde voorstelling, met onderschrift 1796 L 'EGALITE. Op de achtergrond een wijnkelder. Burgelijk leven tijdens de komst van de Fransen in 1795-1796. Zie ook pendant.

artworks.title: The Basilica of Santi Giovanni e Paolo in Rome, with Two Studies of Plants
artworks.medium: paint (coating), mineral, inorganic material, paper, graphite (mineral), watercolor (paint)
artworks.description: The church, bell tower and monastery complex are here rendered from virtually the same vantage point as in Knip’s large watercolour (see adjacent), only from further away. Whether the studies of plants that make up the ‘foreground’ were also drawn in the vicinity of Santi Giovanni e Paolo is doubtful. Knip often combined unrelated motifs on a single sheet of paper.

artworks.date: in or after c. 1660 - in or before c. 1661
artworks.description: Ter Borch depicted a majestic Cecilia, the patron saint of music, playing the organ. Thus, the angel on the left sings along attentively and the winged boy on the right operates the bellows.

View of Ariccia from Genzano
artworks.medium: paint (coating), mineral, inorganic material, paper, graphite (mineral), watercolor (paint)
artworks.description:
Knip drew the town of Ariccia and environs as seen from Genzano on two sheets of paper. Ariccia is dominated by the dome of the church of Santa Maria dell’Annunziata, designed by Bernini. At the right is the Santuario di Santa Maria di Galloro, where a miraculous image of the Virgin Mary, painted on a piece of rock, has been venerated since 1623. In the foreground Knip twice drew a detail of an old paved road,
probably the Appian Way.

Op de voorgrond zijn de twee andere Hollandse schepen te zien die bij het eskader horen: links de Schelde en rechts de Diamand. Ertussen in ligt een schuitje van de Zeepaard, waarschijnlijk richting land varend om vers water in te slaan. Rechts liggen drie Engelse schepen en daarachter een Zweeds schip. In het landschap zijn drie munitieopslagplaatsen weergegeven: links Half Moon Battery, achter de schuit Chubbs Battery en rechts van het tweede Hollandse schip Mundens Battery, gelegen op de rots Ruperts Hill. Rechts van deze rots is het kasteel met zijn rode dak te zien en daarachter de kerktoren van de St Jameskerk.

artworks.description: During the years 1601-1603 Paulus van Vianen worked as Hofgoldschmied (court goldsmith) for the Archbishop of Salzburg. Nothing is known about his metalwork in this period. artworks.title: Minerva as Rome
artworks.description:
The sculptor Algardi mainly drew in preparation for his (portrait) sculptures and reliefs. In the case of this drawing, however, no sculpture is known. It is therefore quite possible that this sheet served as a design for a print. The goddess Minerva, recognizable by her helmet,
personifies Rome here. Depicted at her feet are the city’s founders Romulus and Remus being suckled by a wolf.

artworks.title: Travellers Halted in a Wooded Landscape
artworks.medium: paint (coating), inorganic material, paper, watercolor (paint), chalk
artworks.description: With his balanced landscape compositions and crisply drawn figures, Sandby was a source of inspiration for artists such as William Turner and Michael Rooker. Between 1770 and 1800 Sandby produced many watercolours, like this one, that were meant to be framed and displayed. He had to pay for their framing himself. This became a burden, and so he turned to painting in oil after 1800.

artworks.title: Design Stages for miffy’s letter
artworks.description: This tableau shows the design stages for the book miffy’s letter, in which Miffy goes camping and writes home about her experiences. Once Bruna was satisfied with a sketch, he scored the lines through onto soft paper. He carefully filled the resulting groove with black poster paint, giving rise to a blurred line. These black outlines were then transferred to translucent film and placed over various coloured collages.

Such sheets were often cut into pieces by dealers to increase their profits. The figure at the left is too tightly cropped. It is now unclear whether he is a beggar asking for alms, or perhaps a figure in a historical scene.

artworks.title: An Albino Man with a Fool’s Cap and a Pole Weapon
artworks.description: Andries Beeckman (1628-1664). Andries Beeckman recorded the people he saw on his travels to South Africa and Southeast Asia. As far as we know he drew them from life. Only he probably did not see the Khoikhoi woman with an infant in this way, as he copied her from a drawing in an English travel journal. Beeckman’s drawings found favour with European collectors and he also used them as preliminary studies for his paintings.

artworks.medium: metal, paper, lead (metal), inorganic material, lead and lead alloy, prepared paper, loodstift
artworks.description: Hendrick Goltzius made this preparatory drawing for the engraved portrait of the merchant Jean Niquet in metalpoint, in this case with a lead stylus. Quite unusually he often drew in metalpoint. In his time, this technique had fallen out of favour and people preferred to draw with pen, brush, and chalk. One possible explanation is that Goltzius did this out of admiration for Albrecht Dürer, who had worked a great deal in silverpoint.

artworks.description:
Of old, Tivoli – the Roman ‘Tibur’ – was the place where prosperous city dwellers built country residences to escape the noise and stench of Rome. Dupré made this drawing in the fabled gardens of the Villa d’Este, at the time – and still – one of the
greatest sights in Tivoli. The dome of St. Peter’s basilica is visible between the tree trunks.

artworks.description: A lad steals eggs from a nest. Two peasants watch him closely, so intently in fact that they are oblivious to the boy cutting one of their purses. The depiction may have an erotic significance: whoever stands by idly, will not go far in love. The fish trap in the water could also refer to courtship and marriage.

artworks.title: Peasant Family around the Fireplace
artworks.medium: inorganic material, materials by function, paper, ink, chalk, pencil
artworks.description: A family is gathered about the hearth in a meagre interior. By the fire, the oldest of the girls is drying a cloth. The mother is sitting beside a cradle feeding porridge to the youngest, while father and son look on. It was a favourite theme of Adriaen van Ostade’s, and he often introduced tiny variations: there was evidently considerable demand for these depictions of this simple, yet contented family.

artworks.title: Study for The Battle of Waterloo
artworks.description: Pieneman’s studies depict individual combats more clearly than his large painting. Amid the chaos in the centre of this drawing one man is being despatched by a pistol shot, while another succumbs to a deadly sabre thrust. At the lower left a horse without a rider gallops into the scene, which represents an attack by German mercenaries in Wellington’s army.

artworks.medium: paint (coating), watercolor (paint), biological material, parchment (animal material), gouache (paint)
artworks.description: Commissioned by doctors, Jan l’Admiral made detailed anatomical design drawings, of which he later made prints to illustrate their medical treatises. He probably chose parchment because the ‘living’ character of the material suited the subjects. The skull belonged to an unknown child who died before birth. The skin was that of an Ethiopian woman, which begs the question of how the doctors obtained their study materials.

artworks.description: Andries Beeckman (1628-1664). Andries Beeckman recorded the people he saw on his travels to South Africa and Southeast Asia. As far as we know he drew them from life. Only he probably did not see the Khoikhoi woman with an infant in this way, as he copied her from a drawing in an English travel journal. Beeckman’s drawings found favour with European collectors and he also used them as preliminary studies for his paintings.

perched at a rakish angle on his bewigged head. Hofwijk Manor, near Voorburg, was built to the plans of his father, the statesman, poet and composer Constantijn Huygens I.

artworks.dimensions: height 60.5 cm x width 48.5 cm × weight 8 kg
artworks.description: Under pressure from fierce opposition to his rule, Stadtholder William V and his family fled The Hague in 1785. They returned two years later and the stadtholder’s authority was restored. This provided the occasion to commission a series of portraits of the members of his family from the portraitist Tischbein. The artist produced a fashionable group of oval portraits in pastel. The giltwood frames were made by the Hague framemaker Hendrik Ebbens.

artworks.title: Study of a Gnarled Tree
artworks.description: Paulus van Vianen was appointed ‘Kammergoldschmied’ (court goldsmith) by Emperor Rudolf II in Prague, in 1603. The Utrecht native was not only a phenomenal silversmith but also a gifted draughtsman. Encouraged by his patron to observe raw nature, Van Vianen ventured far and wide. He regularly used the studies he made outdoors to decorate his silver plaques and bowls.

artworks.title: Settlement on a Hill
artworks.description: Domenico Campagnola built up the composition of this hilly landscape diagonally from left to right. Typical of his drawing style is the way in which he suggested shadows with parallel hatching. He left some parts completely empty, such as the sky and passages of the foreground. He had adopted this way of drawing from Titian, one of the great innovators of 16th-century landscape art.

artworks.title: Otter (Lutra lutra)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, watercolor (paint), deck paint, ink
artworks.description: By the 19th century, scholars wished to see how animals lived, so later owner Van Huerne commissioned artists to add background settings to many sheets. Here, not only was land added underneath the otter, but water was depicted in the lower right corner, a requirement to convey the habitat of this predator. Moreover, the animal is now seen flaunting a freshly caught fish in its jaws.

artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, watercolor (paint), deck paint, ink
artworks.description: The later artist who was commissioned by Van Huerne to add settings and backgrounds to many of the drawings here drew an island in a river, namely the Nile (Nilus fluv). With this, he probably wanted to allude to the animal’s name and its natural habitat. The ancient Egyptians considered this ichneumon to be sacred since it is immune to snake poison – hence its nickname ‘pharaoh rat’.

artworks.title: De vloot van de prins in de haven van Hellevoetsluis, 1688
artworks.description: De vloot wordt in de haven van Hellevoetsluis in gereedheid gebracht voor de tocht van prins Willem III met zijn leger naar Engeland, 28 oktober 1688. Een panormabeeld van de vloot van Stadhouder Willem III, met een uitleg in een kader onderin (waar ook de titel), links en rechts een halve palmboom en een gekroond schild met bazuinengelen boven. De vloot lijkt grotendeels klaar te liggen op zee, maar enkele schepen worden nog geladen met kanonnen die klaar liggen op de kade. Vooraan ligt het schip van 'sijn Hoogheijt in het welk waren den Heer van Odijck ende den Marschalk van Schombergh'. Aan de kade schouwt de prins de vloot in gezelschap van de 'den Grave Carel sijn soon ende den Heer dela Caillemotte Soon vande Marquis de Ruvignij '. Links en rechts palmbomen, in de lucht engelen met het wapen van de prins. Ontwerp voor een prent.

artworks.title: Brothel Scene
artworks.description:
This type of scene was called a Bordeeltje (‘little bordello’). The biblical story of the Prodigal Son squandering his inheritance was a popular pretext for painting brothel scenes. Knüpfer regularly depicted biblical scenes, which led to attributing this drawing to him. Yet the Prodigal
Son seems to be missing here. At the right can be seen the old procuress, who ensures that her girls keep the men’s spirits up.

artworks.artist: Anselmus Boëtius de Boodt (signed by artist)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), materials by function, paper, watercolor (paint), deck paint, ink, pencil
artworks.description: De Boodt could study many live animals from far-flung places in Rudolf II’s menagerie, as well as numerous stuffed creatures in his unstkammer. Even so, many drawings in De Boodt’s albums were not made from direct observation of nature but were ‘borrowed’ from illustrations by other artists. The comically sad look of this zorilla suggests that this image was copied from a pre-existing source.

artworks.title: Trumpeter on Horseback
artworks.medium: inorganic material, materials by function, paper, chalk, ink
artworks.description: As indicated by the later inscription at the upper left, this drawing of a flamboyant trumpeter was long ascribed to Rembrandt. In point of fact, the draughtsman was his contemporary Jan Lievens. When he made this ambitious drawing, Lievens was possibly sharing a workshop with Rembrandt in Leiden. Lievens had also trained with Lastman, well before Rembrandt, between around 1617 and 1619.

artworks.title: Dipakali ragini
artworks.dimensions: height 228 mm x width 160 mm × height 260 mm x width 193 mm
artworks.description: In een overdekte ruimte van een paleis zit Krishna op een rolkussen, links voor hem een jonge vrouw gehurkt, beide handen tegen elkaar naar voren gestrekt; achter haar tegen de muur een brandend olielampje; links voor de muur van het paleis drie vrouwen, de voorste danst, de middelste bespeelt een trommel en de achterste houdt een schaaltje vast, boven de muur van het paleis een nachtelijke sterrenhemel met een maansikkel. Rond de voorstelling twee biezen in kaderlijnen, de ene geel en de buitenste, bredere rood; het koepeldak van het paleis en de derde vrouw links zijn deels over deze biezen heen geschilderd.

artworks.title: William George Frederick, Prince of Orange-Nassau (Youngest Son of William V)
artworks.medium: chalk, biological material, inorganic material, parchment (animal material), pastel (crayon)
artworks.dimensions: height 60.5 cm x width 49 cm × weight 9.3 kg
artworks.description: Under pressure from fierce opposition to his rule, Stadtholder William V and his family fled The Hague in 1785. They returned two years later and the stadtholder’s authority was restored. This provided the occasion to commission a series of portraits of the members of his family from the portraitist Tischbein. The artist produced a fashionable group of oval portraits in pastel. The giltwood frames were made by the Hague framemaker Hendrik Ebbens.

artworks.title: Ontwerp voor een bord met WB
King David’s Sacrifice
artworks.description:
Felice Giani was a productive painter who decorated rooms with colourful history scenes. This drawing was probably made on commission. Neoclassically oriented artists hardly ever chose scenes from the Old Testament as subjects. Here we see God – in the guise of an angel with an
olive branch – finally reconciling with King David during a sacrificial offering. No painting or fresco by Giani of this theme is known.

artworks.description: Andries Beeckman (1628-1664). Andries Beeckman recorded the people he saw on his travels to South Africa and Southeast Asia. As far as we know he drew them from life. Beeckman’s drawings found favour with European collectors and he also used them as preliminary studies for his paintings.

artworks.title: Snapdragon Plant with Seed Pods (Antirrhinum majus L.)
artworks.medium: paint (coating), inorganic material, materials by function, paper, watercolor (paint), deck paint, chalk, ink
artworks.description:
The Historia Naturalis aimed to give a reliable scientific image for each subject, but at first sight this strangelooking plant seems rather fantastical. However, the skull-like white ‘flowers’ are the dried seed pods of the snapdragon. The draughtsman copied the image from a
print from the Cruydt-Boeck (1554), an album with plant illustrations made by botanist Rembert Dodoens (1517-1585).

artworks.title: Album met aquarellen en tekeningen van reisgezichten in Zuid-Italië en op Sicilië en Malta
artworks.dimensions: height 655 mm x width 520 mm x thickness 55 mm
artworks.description: Album met leren band met goudopdruk waarin aquarellen en tekeningen van reisgezichten in Zuid-Italië en op Sicilië en Malta. Op 26 januari 1778 verlieten Willem Carel Dierkens en Willem Hendrik van Nieuwerkerke Den Haag voor een reis naar Zuid-Italië, Sicilië en Malta. Later sloten ook Nicolaas ten Hove, Nathaniel Thornbury en de Zwitserse kunstenaar Louis Ducros zich bij hen aan. Ducros legde onderweg de bezienswaardigheden vast, welke door Ten Hove thuis na de reis werden gemonteerd in drie albums. Dit eerste album bevat tekeningen van landschappen, stadsgezichten, antieke monumenten en scènes uit het dagelijks leven onderweg.

artworks.description: Rooker excelled in the rendering of buildings. He did not use lines drawn in pen, but rather only a brush and ink or watercolour. Glastonbury Abbey had been very prosperous until King Henry VIII dissolved all of the monasteries in 1536, after which most of them gradually went to ruin.

artworks.title: Marskramer demonstreert zijn koopwaar
artworks.description:
The hawker, in the right foreground, plays a Jew’s harp – also called a trompe (or trump) – a primitive musical instrument. Although his wife tries to stop him, the man at the left is keen to buy such a trifle and reaches into his purse. In the 17th-century ‘Iemand trompen
verkopen’ (to sell someone trumps) meant ‘to deceive someone’. Poor customer, he is buying a worthless piece of junk.

artworks.title: Portret van een (gefantaseerd?) Engels schip met Justitia op de spiegel
artworks.description: Portret van een (gefantaseerd?) Engels schip met Justitia op de spiegel. Dat dit een tegendruk is, blijkt onder meer uit het feit dat de letters R en C en het wapen van Engeland, de Stuart Royal Standard, in spiegelbeeld zijn. De letters moeten dus worden gelezen als CR (Carolus Rex). Het is niet uit te sluiten dat dit een fantasieschip is. De tekening vertoont namelijk grote overeenkomsten met twee andere opgewerkte tegendrukken van de oude Van de Velde in Rotterdam, waarvan er één het opschrift draagt: vervolgende schepen heeft vande velde / naer eÿgen fantazÿen geordineert / & geschiert. De Engelse fantasieschepen in Rotterdam hebben net als de tekening in het Rijksprentenkabinet een sculptuur van vrouwe Justitia, herkenbaar aan zwaard en weegschaal, op de spiegel. Er zijn meer tegendrukken van Engelse schepen die waarschijnlijk door Van de Velde zelf zijn bedacht. Een aantal daarvan is op papier met hetzelfde watermerk als de hier beschreven tekening, een merk dat vooral in de tweede helft van de jaren zestig wordt aangetroffen, maar incidenteel ook rond 1672-73. Door Muller gerelateerd aan de tocht naar Chatham, 1667.

artworks.description: Charles Parrocel was a cavalryman in his younger years and thus knew the military world inside out. artworks.title: Frontispiece Design for De wonderlyke reizen van Fernando Mendez Pinto
artworks.description:
Fortune takes centre stage, and is depicted nude, as was customary at the time. She rests one foot on a globe as a sign that fortune is fickle and one can quickly fall from grace. The man at her side and the seascape in the background represent misfortune. All kinds of instruments
of torture are being cast over him. The woman at the right with the horn of plenty personifies Prosperity.

artworks.title: Frontispiece Design for Frederick Hendrick van Nassauw
artworks.medium: paint (coating), inorganic material, materials by function, paper, deck paint, ink, chalk
artworks.description: This second, worked out drawing served as the model for the engraver. In this definitive design it is clear to see that Mars, the god of war, presents a sword to Frederick Henry. Above them, Fame trumpets the prince’s glory. Concord, with arrows representing the seven Dutch provinces, Navigation, the provider of wealth, and Liberty with her hat on a stick can also be recognized.

artworks.medium: paint (coating), mineral, inorganic material, paper, graphite (mineral), watercolor (paint)
artworks.description: On the lower part of this drawing (now cut in half) Knip wrote ‘First sheet of the three marked Q’. Inscriptions like this are found on a number of his drawings. It was the artist’s way of indicating that two or three sheets formed a cohesive group. The drawings can sometimes be joined up to form a continuous panorama, as is the case with this view from the Villa Mattei (now Villa Celimontana) in Rome.
